# AGENTS.md

Respond to the user in clear, concise and polite Japanese.

**pqc-scan** is a Rust CLI static analyzer of Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC)
migration risks. It scans repositories for cryptographic usage using rules and
produces migration reports. Security, correctness, backward compatibility and
stable output are critical.

## Working Approach

Apply instructions by their purpose: **Constraints** are mandatory boundaries;
**Outcomes** are required results; **Guidance** recommends methods within those
boundaries; **Verification** defines required evidence and completion gates.
This distinction does not downgrade existing requirements or create exceptions.

- The main agent investigates, plans, implements, debugs, tests, evaluates and
  documents. Planner, Executor and Evaluator are responsibilities, not processes
  or separate prompts. The only review prompt is `docs/agent/REVIEWER.md`.
- Prefer small, safe changes; avoid unrelated refactoring and preserve user edits.
- Clear, small changes need no separate design or implementation plan.
  Explanations, research and small changes need no separate task record.
- For complex or ambiguous work, first summarize purpose, acceptance criteria,
  constraints, compatibility, viable approaches, recommendation, steps and checks.
- Reuse applicable plans, task records and evidence. Ask about unresolved decisions
  materially affecting correctness, compatibility, security or scope; continue
  authorized work that does not depend on them.
- For authorized work, continue through implementation, applicable tests,
  required reviews, fixes and final verification without asking for approval at
  each stage. Resolve minor, reversible choices within scope; a plan or first
  implementation alone does not fulfill an implementation request.
- Do not change agreed scope or acceptance criteria without explicit agreement.
- Do not select unrelated work or create tasks because the queue is empty.
  Task creation and scope expansion require authorization. Report out-of-scope
  findings as proposals, not new tasks.
- Monitor only explicitly requested signals within the authorized scope and
  duration. Do not automatically generate tasks from reflection or monitoring.
- Saved plans, handoffs and skills must obey these limits and completion gates.
- Identify unresolved instruction conflicts before performing dependent work.
- When a rule or skill requires a pause or human decision, identify and link the
  exact source, quote the relevant instruction and explain the decision needed.
  Distinguish an explicit requirement from interpretation; complete independent,
  authorized preparation without crossing the approval boundary. Skills do not
  authorize scope expansion, delegation or bypassing repository constraints.

## Required References by Activity

This file and the applicable documents below define mandatory working rules.
The table is for the main agent; reviewers follow the scoped reading policy in
[review details](docs/agent/REVIEWS.md). Before the corresponding activity, read
its references; combine rows when several apply. References are not automatically
loaded: open them explicitly. If scope expands, read newly applicable references
before the affected work.

| Activity | Required references |
|---|---|
| Any repository work | This file; selected task, original acceptance criteria and applicable plans, if any |
| Any change; verification; completion decision | [Verification by change type](docs/agent/VERIFICATION.md#verification-by-change-type), evidence and completion rules in that guide |
| Product implementation, Rust tests, Cargo, rules, CI, scripts or packaging changes | [Best practices](docs/BEST-PRACTICES.md); relevant sections of [patterns by activity](docs/PATTERNS.md#activity-index) and [known mistakes](docs/MISTAKES.md) |
| Understanding or changing product behavior, components or interfaces | Relevant sections of [English README](README.md#features), [Japanese README](README.ja.md#features), [architecture](docs/architecture.md#workspace-modules), and affected user guides/designs |
| Design or architecture decisions | Relevant sections of [architecture](docs/architecture.md#workspace-modules), recorded decisions in the [decision log](docs/DECISIONS.md), [patterns by activity](docs/PATTERNS.md#activity-index) and [known mistakes](docs/MISTAKES.md); use the decision template only when recording an agreed decision |
| User implementation request; independent review or material follow-up | [Review policy](docs/agent/REVIEWS.md#required-review-stages); reviewers also read this file, [review template](docs/agent/REVIEWER.md) and their review package |
| Creating, updating, resuming or closing task records | [Task lifecycle definitions](docs/TASK-LIFECYCLE.md#status-definitions) and [task layout and fields](tasks/README.md) |
| Rule changes | [Rule validation and quality review](docs/rules-reference.md#validation-and-quality-review) and affected rule entries |
| Report content, presentation, interaction or browser acceptance | [Report content](docs/agent/REPORTS.md#user-facing-report-content) and [browser verification](docs/agent/REPORTS.md#local-report-browser-verification), plus affected report/user/design documentation |
| Agent guidance or workflow documentation changes | [Documentation best practices](docs/BEST-PRACTICES.md#documentation), [documentation synchronization](docs/PATTERNS.md#documentation-synchronization-pattern), and every affected current guidance document |
| Restart baseline or task 014 only, unless explicitly extended by the user | [Restart loop](docs/RESTART-LOOP.md) |

- Read required material once per session and reuse it; revisit changed or
  uncertain sections. Use targeted searches, not repeated whole-directory reads.
  Linked headings are entry points; read all other applicable sections, not only
  the landing section.
- After compaction or handoff, restore scope, decisions, evidence, reviewer IDs
  and next actions from the existing task record or handoff before reinvestigating.
- Conditional reading never reduces required verification or relevant evidence.
- Apply restart-loop entry, retry, status-transition and completion gates only
  within its stated scope; monitoring and automatic task creation remain disabled
  during that pilot.

## Workflow and Review Limits

1. Establish outcome, original criteria, applicable task and existing evidence.
2. Implement minimal changes and meaningful tests, run initial checks and inspect
   the combined diff before implementation review.
3. Obtain required implementation review, fix findings, complete required tests,
   then obtain required test review. Resolve findings and verify final-source evidence.
4. Apply all completion gates; record durable lessons in existing knowledge docs
   only when useful. Explanations, research and small changes need not use every step.

- Main-agent investigation, design, implementation, testing and documentation
  must not be delegated. Explanations, research, design proposals and
  documentation-only changes do not automatically require review subagents.
- Requests changing product code, tests, rules, Cargo/dependencies, CI, scripts,
  packaging or other executable behavior require two independent stages:
  implementation review after implementation, then test review after required tests.
  Prose-only documentation changes are normally exempt; mixed requests and
  executable examples require both stages. Explicit review requirements still apply.
- Use at most two reviewer identities per request, one per stage. Review the
  combined change; reuse each reviewer for material fixes. Reviewers cannot delegate.
- Extra agents require explicit user authorization of purpose and maximum count.
  Tools, task count and generic skill/delegation wording are not authorization.
- Splitting plans, fixing findings, resuming or handing off never resets the budget.
- Follow [review details](docs/agent/REVIEWS.md), including isolated reviewer context,
  evidence, [recording without a task](docs/agent/REVIEWS.md#review-records),
  reviewer continuity and scoped confirmation after material fixes.
- Tasks live in `tasks/<ID>/task.yaml`; plans, results and reviews belong in the
  same task directory, with raw evidence under `evidence/`. Normal states are
  pending → planned → in-progress
  → review → done; blocked and cancelled are distinct optional states. Follow
  [task lifecycle](docs/TASK-LIFECYCLE.md) for transitions, failures and resumption.
- Default to one task per PR, including implementation, tests and docs. Plan steps
  do not create separate tasks, PRs or reviewers. Keep prerequisite feasibility
  studies separate when their results determine whether/how implementation proceeds.

## Security and Compatibility

- Validate inputs; never expose secrets, private key material or sensitive
  cryptographic data in output or logs. Never weaken cryptographic checks.
- Preserve cryptographic integrity, API compatibility and external output contracts.
- An absent detection is not proof of safety or full support unless specified.
- Rules are in `rules/default/*.yml`: maintain unique IDs and valid schemas, test
  matching/non-matching inputs, assess compatibility and update the reference as needed.

Stop affected work and obtain human review for:

- high-risk architectural changes;
- cryptographic logic changes without a clear specification;
- rule changes that could break compatibility;
- storage format changes.

Preserve work and evidence; explain the required decision before proceeding.
Human review is separate from independent reviews and grants no extra agent slots.

## Documentation

- Maintain English and Japanese versions of end-user documentation: the root
  `README.md` (English), root `README.ja.md` (Japanese), and documents under
  `docs/user/`. Keep paired versions factually consistent and update both for
  user-facing behavior changes. Report format changes also require applicable
  report docs, subject to the human review conditions above.
- Write developer-only documentation in English: `tasks/`, `docs/agent/`,
  `docs/quality/`, `docs/records/`, `docs/roadmap/`, `docs/architecture/`,
  `docs/product/`, `docs/releases/`, and all other files under `docs/` outside
  `docs/user/`. This includes explanatory prose in task definitions and results.
- Apply these language rules to newly authored or revised explanatory prose.
  Do not translate code, commands, identifiers, paths, structured data or quoted
  material to satisfy this policy. These rules do not change the requirement to
  communicate with the user in Japanese.
- Update affected agent references together when terms or paths change.
- This file owns core constraints and summarizes detailed rules. Linked guides
  own verification/completion (`docs/agent/VERIFICATION.md`), reviews
  (`docs/agent/REVIEWS.md`), reports (`docs/agent/REPORTS.md`) and task lifecycle
  (`docs/TASK-LIFECYCLE.md`) details. Core constraints always apply; update affected
  summaries, details and references together in the same change. Resolve conflicts
  before dependent work; neither location permits weakening the other's constraints.
- Preserve past reviews, completed tasks and measurements, including their
  original languages and wording; the language policy does not authorize
  translating or rewriting historical records or evidence. Historical role names
  and paths describe their time, not instructions to restore removed prompts.
- Use existing knowledge documents for durable lessons; avoid duplicate knowledge
  and unnecessary design/reflection docs. Documentation never replaces validation.

## Completion and Communication

- Use `rust-toolchain.toml` and the applicable checks in
  [verification rules](docs/agent/VERIFICATION.md); optional features need their
  own applicable checks. Documentation-only work normally needs no Rust checks.
- Mark done only when every original criterion/deliverable is implemented and
  verified against final source, including required reviews. Partial, Unknown,
  Not Tested, failed or deferred required work prevents completion.
- Artifact lists, passing logs or limited reviews do not cover requirements
  outside their scope. Never narrow criteria or move work elsewhere to claim done.
- Evaluation completion and measured product quality are different; incomplete
  truth, missing measurements and unverified assessment validity stay unfinished.
- Continue resolvable work. For blockers, keep work unfinished and record the
  dependency, attempts, unmet criteria and concrete action/decision needed.
- Base retries on a correction, new evidence or a changed approach; do not repeat
  an unchanged failed attempt without a reason to expect progress. Preserve any
  applicable task-specific retry limits and keep blocked work unfinished.
- Reopening incorrectly closed work preserves history and reconciles queue/roadmap;
  cancellation requires a maintainer decision and reopening an explicit new request.
- Report in concise, polite Japanese: resulting behavior, why it changed, actual
  verification and remaining work. Distinguish implementation, measurements,
  proposals and unexecuted checks. Provide source version, commands, exit results
  and artifact links for changes/measurements; summarize routine successful checks.
- Claim completion only against original criteria. Lead partial results with the
  unfinished status and reason; never describe unfinished work as complete.

# Verification and Completion

These are mandatory details of [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md). Read this file
before any change and before claiming completion, including documentation-only
work. Apply every relevant change category; overlapping categories accumulate.

# Development and Verification

Use the Rust toolchain specified in `rust-toolchain.toml`.

Typical commands:

```bash
cargo build --workspace
cargo test --workspace
cargo fmt --all
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

Example CLI run:

```bash
cargo run --bin pqc-scan -- scan ./examples \
  --format all \
  --out-dir ./target/pqc-report \
  --rules-dir ./rules
```

## Verification by Change Type

During development, use targeted checks to diagnose and validate the affected
behavior. Before completion, every applicable requirement below and every
task-specific acceptance check needs passing evidence for the final source.
Targeted success alone does not replace required broader checks.

For Rust implementation, Rust tests, Cargo configuration or dependency changes:

- Run relevant targeted tests during development.
- Run `cargo fmt --all` and inspect resulting changes.
- Run `cargo test --workspace`.
- Run `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Run `cargo build --workspace` when validating executable behavior,
  packaging or a required build deliverable.
- Exercise affected optional features and supported configurations.
  Default workspace tests do not establish coverage of disabled features.

For rule changes:

- Validate rule schema and unique IDs.
- Run relevant positive and negative detection tests.
- Run workspace tests and required task-specific acceptance checks.
- Run Rust checks above when Rust source or test code also changes.

For documentation-only changes:

- Check references, links, commands and consistency with actual behavior.
- Check agreement between English and Japanese documentation where applicable.
- Rust builds and tests are not required unless the documentation change
  affects executable examples or its acceptance criteria require them.

For CI, scripts or packaging changes:

- Run the relevant syntax checks, script tests and packaging checks.
- Validate affected workflows or produced artifacts as required.
- Local checks do not substitute for required CI execution.

For user-facing behavior:

- Exercise the affected CLI or report workflow.
- Verify compatibility and relevant error paths.
- Follow the browser verification requirements for report presentation
  or interaction changes.

## Verification Evidence

- Record the source revision, relevant uncommitted changes, command,
  feature configuration and exit result.
- Preserve logs or artifacts needed to assess required acceptance criteria.
- A HEAD SHA alone is insufficient when the worktree contains tested changes.
- Reuse passing results while their source, inputs and environment remain
  applicable. Repeat checks when changes or unresolved concerns invalidate them.
- Once required checks have applicable passing evidence, do not repeat or broaden
  checks without a changed input, new requirement or unresolved concern. Assess
  applicability using the reuse rules below; this does not waive required checks.
- Do not write tests that merely mirror implementation details.
- Use assertions that establish observable requirements and relevant failures.
- Do not claim an unexecuted, unavailable or failed check passed.

## Reusing Evidence After Changes

Compare final source, inputs, configuration and environment with the recorded run.
Record why each reused result remains applicable; uncertainty requires the
affected checks to run again. These examples do not waive any required check:

| Later change | Evidence to reassess |
|---|---|
| Prose or comments only | Check links, commands and consistency; product execution results may remain applicable if behavior, executable examples and build/test inputs are unchanged. |
| Tests or fixtures only | Rerun changed tests and checks that consume those inputs; reassess whether earlier coverage conclusions still hold. |
| Product or shared helper logic | Rerun affected behavior, failure and compatibility checks, including dependent callers; shared impact may require the full suite. |
| Dependencies, features, toolchain or environment | Reassess every result that depends on them; rerun the affected configurations, builds and acceptance checks. |

Checks required by the change categories above must have applicable passing
evidence for final source. An unchanged file alone does not establish this:
dependencies, generated inputs and invoked binaries can change its behavior.
Use the [review revision rules](REVIEWS.md#revisions-and-resumption) to determine
whether the existing reviewer must confirm affected conclusions.

# Completion and Partial Results

Mark a task `done` only when every original acceptance criterion and required
deliverable has been implemented and verified with evidence matching the
final source, including the required review stages.

- An artifact list, passing tests or a limited review does not establish
  completion of requirements outside its scope.
- Do not mark a task done while required work is Partial, Unknown, Not Tested,
  failed or deferred.
- Recording a limitation or transferring work to another task does not satisfy
  the original criterion.
- Do not narrow acceptance criteria or reinterpret scope without explicit
  user agreement.
- Distinguish completion of an evaluation from measured product quality.
  Finding a product failure can be a valid completed evaluation only when
  the evaluation itself is complete and valid for every required criterion.
- Incomplete truth, missing measurements, unresolved required reviews and
  unverified assessment validity remain unfinished work.
- Continue work on resolvable issues.
- If a blocker prevents completion, keep the task unfinished and explain:
  - what is blocked and why
  - what was attempted
  - which acceptance criteria remain unmet
  - the concrete action or decision needed to proceed
- When reopening an incorrectly closed task, preserve historical evidence,
  record why the previous completion decision is superseded, and reconcile
  the task queue and roadmap without rewriting old measurements.
- Cancellation is an explicit maintainer decision, not implementation completion.
  Preserve its reason and history. Reopening requires an explicit new request.

# Independent Review Request Template

The main agent fills the request below for each required review stage and sends
it to that stage's reviewer. Use the same template for both stages; do not combine
reviewer identities. Read [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) and the
[review policy](REVIEWS.md) for criteria, budget and revision handling.

## Request

- Stage: implementation review or test review
- Requirements: original acceptance criteria, scope and compatibility constraints
- Source: baseline/current revision and relevant uncommitted changes
- Change: relevant diff or diff artifact, affected files and pre-existing changes
- Evidence: commands, features/configurations, results and artifact paths
- Gaps: failed, unavailable or unexecuted required checks
- Follow-up, if applicable: previously reviewed source, changes since that review,
  resolved/unresolved findings, affected conclusions, rerun checks and reasons
  that reused evidence still applies

## Reviewer Instructions

- Apply the assigned stage's criteria in `docs/agent/REVIEWS.md` and the applicable
  completion/verification gates in `docs/agent/VERIFICATION.md`. Read additional
  source or documentation only as needed to evaluate the supplied scope.
- Do not modify files or delegate. Rely on supplied test results unless a
  specific concern requires independent reproduction; do not automatically
  repeat the full suite.
- For follow-up, check material fixes and whether evidence covers the final
  source. Do not assume an earlier review covers later changes.
- For prose-only guidance changes requiring review, implementation review checks
  instruction meaning, reference relationships and preservation of mandatory
  gates. Test review checks whether structural and consistency verification
  establishes those requirements for the final source. Structural checks alone
  do not demonstrate improved agent execution performance.

## Response

- Reviewed stage, source version and scope
- Actionable findings: severity, file/line, requirement impact and reasoning
- Material coverage gaps or unknowns, including missing required evidence
- Acceptance decision for the assigned scope, with reasons

Explicitly state when no actionable findings were identified. Review acceptance
is not task completion; the main agent applies all completion gates in AGENTS.md.

# Independent Reviews

These are mandatory details of [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md). Read this file before
starting a user implementation request. At each review stage or material follow-up,
confirm the applicable rules using the [reading-reuse policy](../../AGENTS.md#required-references-by-activity);
reread only changed or uncertain sections. Reviewers read it with AGENTS.md,
[docs/agent/REVIEWER.md](REVIEWER.md) and the supplied review package.
The main agent's full reading list is not a reviewer checklist; reviewers consult
additional source and documents only as needed for their assigned scope.

# Subagent and Token Policy

## Main-Agent Responsibilities

The main agent performs investigation, design, planning, implementation,
debugging, testing and documentation without delegating them to subagents.

Explanations, research, design proposals and documentation-only changes
do not automatically require independent review subagents.

## Required Review Stages

For this policy, a user implementation request includes changes to product code,
tests, detection rules, Cargo configuration or dependencies, CI, scripts,
packaging, executable examples or other executable behavior, regardless of file
extension. A request mixing these with documentation follows both stages for the
combined change. Small implementation changes are not exempt.

Explanations, research, design proposals and prose-only documentation changes
normally require neither stage unless the original acceptance criteria or an
explicit user instruction require review. This exception does not waive applicable
verification, safety, compatibility or human-review gates.

Use two review stages for each user implementation request in this scope:

1. Implementation review:
   - After implementation, start one implementation-review subagent.
   - Review the combined change for correctness, requirements, security,
     architecture consistency and compatibility.
   - Supply available test results and identify checks that remain unexecuted.

2. Test review:
   - After the main agent completes required tests, start one test-review
     subagent.
   - Check whether the tests actually verify the final change.
   - Inspect coverage, relevant positive and negative cases, meaningful
     assertions, commands, features and evidence matching the final source.
   - Passing logs alone do not establish adequate testing.

The main agent fixes findings and runs necessary verification.

## Review Budget and Context

- Use at most two reviewer identities per user implementation request:
  one for each stage.
- Review the combined change rather than starting reviewers for individual
  plan steps, files, edits, test commands or log files.
- Design, task, branch, final and pre-merge reviews do not create additional
  review slots.
- Reuse each stage's reviewer for scoped verification of material fixes.
- Batch related findings and follow-up requests.
- Reviewers must not delegate further.
- Any additional subagent requires explicit user authorization covering
  its purpose and maximum agent count.
- Tool availability, task count and generic skill wording are not authorization.

When starting a reviewer:

- Use `fork_turns: "none"`.
- Provide concise requirements, the relevant diff or diff artifact,
  source version and test evidence.
- Identify relevant pre-existing changes and exclude unrelated work.
- Do not copy the whole conversation.
- Request actionable findings with file references and requirement impact.

Reviewers rely on the main agent's test evidence unless a specific concern
requires independent reproduction. Do not automatically repeat the full suite.

## Review Records

Record each reviewer's ID, assigned stage, scope, reviewed source version,
decision and unresolved findings in the existing task record or handoff.
Include relevant uncommitted changes; HEAD alone cannot identify a dirty source.
For work without a task record, use an existing PR description or review thread;
before a PR exists, keep a concise handoff in the current chat. Carry that record
forward when opening a PR or moving to another chat. Do not create a task or a
separate document solely to store review metadata. Include evidence paths,
unexecuted checks and the next action so resumption does not require the original
reviewer's conversation.

## Revisions and Resumption

- Splitting a plan, fixing findings, resuming a chat or handing off work
  does not reset the review budget.
- After review-driven changes, rerun affected checks and determine whether
  prior review evidence still applies.
- Obtain scoped confirmation from the existing reviewer when changes
  materially affect the reviewed conclusions.
- A test-review-driven product change must also receive scoped
  implementation review when it affects correctness or compatibility.
- Do not claim an earlier review covers later changes without checking them.
- If a reviewer cannot be resumed, preserve their record and keep affected work
  unfinished. A replacement is another reviewer identity and requires explicit
  user authorization of its purpose and maximum additional count before starting
  it. Do not reset the budget or replace independent review with self-review.

# Patterns

This document captures recurring repository-specific design and implementation patterns.
Use it to understand how this codebase is typically extended.
For normative rules and contributor expectations, see `docs/BEST-PRACTICES.md`.

## Activity Index

Start with the affected area's entries; follow other relevant sections as needed.
These links locate guidance, not an exhaustive checklist or a waiver of required reading.

| Activity | Starting sections |
|---|---|
| CLI | [Thin entrypoints](#thin-cli-entrypoints); [CLI testability lesson](MISTAKES.md#cli-testability) |
| Pipeline or detectors | [Pipeline](#pipeline-centered-scanning); [detector extensions](#detector-extension-pattern); [redaction](#export-redaction-after-stable-identity-task-029) |
| Rules | [Rule-driven matching](#rule-driven-matching) |
| Reports or output contracts | [Writers](#report-writer-extension-pattern); [contract tests](#report-contract-test-pattern); [fact binding](#bind-comparisons-and-human-assessments-to-actual-facts); [export semantics](#preserve-standards-semantics-through-explicit-export-loss) |
| Guidance or task layout | [Documentation synchronization](#documentation-synchronization-pattern); [task queue](#task-queue-pattern); [documentation drift lesson](MISTAKES.md#documentation-drift) |
| Feature or coverage measurements | [Shared target-directory lesson](MISTAKES.md#shared-target-directories-can-invalidate-feature-specific-protocol-evidence); [coverage collection lesson](MISTAKES.md#llvm-coverage-counters-need-a-bounded-and-attributable-collection-path) |

---

## Thin CLI Entrypoints

Pattern:
- keep `main` focused on argument parsing, top-level error reporting, and process exit
- move command behavior into helpers that return explicit results or exit status values

Why it works here:
- CLI behavior stays compatible while remaining easy to test
- stdout and stderr can be asserted without spawning a subprocess

Current example:
- `crates/pqc_scan_cli/src/main.rs`

---

## Pipeline-Centered Scanning

Pattern:
- keep orchestration in the core pipeline
- let repository walking, detection, normalization, recommendation enrichment, and reporting remain distinct stages

Why it works here:
- security-sensitive logic stays inspectable
- new detection capabilities can be added without rewriting the whole scan flow

Current example:
- `crates/pqc_scan_core/src/pipeline.rs`
- `crates/pqc_scan_core/src/walker.rs`

---

## Detector Extension Pattern

Pattern:
- implement the shared detector trait
- keep detector-specific parsing and matching local to the detector crate
- register new detectors through the default detector list rather than wiring them ad hoc
- add targeted tests for both detection hits and sensitive-output handling when a detector touches key or certificate material
- when a detector parses multiple manifest families, keep representative tests for manifest, lockfile, and SBOM inputs so inventory metadata stays stable

Why it works here:
- new detector kinds remain isolated
- the scan pipeline can treat detectors uniformly
- regressions in masking or fallback behavior are caught close to the detector implementation

Current example:
- `crates/pqc_scan_detectors/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/pqc_scan_detectors/src/regex_detector.rs`
- `crates/pqc_scan_detectors/src/tree_sitter_detector.rs`

---

## Rule-Driven Matching

Pattern:
- encode detection logic in YAML rules where possible
- compile and validate rule data at load time
- keep rule IDs unique and update rule reference docs with rule changes

Why it works here:
- detection coverage can evolve without invasive code changes
- invalid rules fail early instead of producing silent scan drift

Current example:
- `crates/pqc_scan_rules/src/lib.rs`
- `rules/default/*.yml`
- `docs/rules-reference.md`

---

## Report Writer Extension Pattern

Pattern:
- add new output formats in the reporting crate
- keep sanitization centralized before format-specific rendering
- preserve existing output paths and field stability unless a planned compatibility change is approved

Why it works here:
- sensitive data handling remains consistent across formats
- downstream tooling can rely on stable report contracts

Current example:
- `crates/pqc_scan_report/src/lib.rs`
- `crates/pqc_scan_report/src/json_report.rs`
- `crates/pqc_scan_report/src/sarif_report.rs`

---

## Report Contract Test Pattern

Pattern:
- keep deterministic writer-level tests next to JSON, HTML, and Markdown report generators
- assert grouped finding rendering, format-specific escaping, stable serialized field names, recommended-action sections, and masked evidence output
- cover inventory-oriented outputs such as `cbom.json` and `dependency-sbom.json` when report contracts are extended
- use synthetic findings with masked placeholders instead of raw sensitive fixtures

Why it works here:
- report outputs are compatibility surfaces and can regress during refactors even when core finding data stays correct
- escaping and masking behavior are security-sensitive and should be checked in the final rendered format, not only in lower-level helpers

Current example:
- `crates/pqc_scan_report/src/json_report.rs`
- `crates/pqc_scan_report/src/html_report.rs`
- `crates/pqc_scan_report/src/markdown_report.rs`

---

## Documentation Synchronization Pattern

Pattern:
- when renaming docs or changing workflow terms, update all agent-facing references in the same patch
- keep core working rules and activity-based reading triggers in `AGENTS.md`, detailed verification/review/report rules in `docs/agent/`, and the shared review request template in `docs/agent/REVIEWER.md`
- treat `AGENTS.md` as the owner of core constraints and the linked guides as owners of detailed procedures; update affected summaries, details and references in the same change, preserving constraints in both
- keep the lifecycle summary in `AGENTS.md` aligned with detailed definitions in `docs/TASK-LIFECYCLE.md`; link to those definitions from `tasks/README.md` rather than duplicating them
- preserve completed task records and past review evidence, including historical prompt paths

Why it works here:
- agents depend on these files as operational inputs
- inconsistent wording causes workflow mistakes and duplicate repair work

Current example:
- `AGENTS.md`
- `docs/TASK-LIFECYCLE.md`
- `docs/agent/REVIEWER.md`

---

## Task Queue Pattern

Pattern:
- keep each task definition in `tasks/<ID>/task.yaml`, with plans, results and reviews beside it and raw evidence under `tasks/<ID>/evidence/`
- discover only the numbered task directories and their direct `task.yaml`; do not treat YAML inside evidence as task definitions
- keep tasks small; responsibility labels describe work performed by the main agent
- let Planner move tasks to `planned`, Executor to `in-progress`, Reviewer review the implementation, and Evaluator close the loop with `done`
- use `blocked` when progress depends on unavailable validation or human decisions

Why it works here:
- responsibilities stay auditable
- unfinished work remains visible without overloading normal completion states

## Export redaction after stable identity (task 029)

Use source positions collected before detector callbacks to protect recognized
private/credential context, then sanitize after legacy IDs and native associations
are built. A truncated preview can lose the syntax needed for later redaction;
mask its context conservatively and test middle fragments as well as whole canaries.
Keep legacy CBOM rows and resolve column-less collisions in favor of masking.
See [the bounded privacy contract](architecture/EVIDENCE-PRIVACY.md).

## Bind comparisons and human assessments to actual facts

A run ID alone does not bind a policy report to immutable inventory content.
Validate the assessment against the actual inventory and selected local context
before rendering it. For heuristic moves, count ambiguous observations before
filtering eligible candidates, and compare referenced asset facts as well as IDs.
An ambiguous or incomplete observation set must preserve uncertainty.

## Preserve standards semantics through explicit export loss

Schema validation verifies shape, not the meaning of a digest, version or
assurance claim. Keep a full-certificate DER hash in a named provenance property
when a standard field requires a different digest input. Omit unsupported standard
fields and record the loss. Preserve source-column units with their values.
